description: Control-arm register for the 19 literature-supported inputs of the minimum HOMER scenario. Values come from public techno-economic datasets and software documentation (NREL, now NLR, ATB 2024 and battery cost projections 2025; IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs; PNNL Energy Storage Grid Cost and Performance 2022; BloombergNEF battery price surveys; HOMER Pro documentation; manufacturer data), deliberately not regional and not aquaculture-specific. Bounds are the range the sources support, not a confidence interval. Every row is a candidate for the human gate. Regional data points are recorded in regional_note for the treatment arm and are not used in the control values.
method_note: Research assisted by AI agents that opened each source and recorded the locator; every value was then checked and the bounds and basis set by the responsible author. Where a source reports at a different boundary (for example AC versus DC nameplate, or a total system including the power conversion system), the conversion is stated in basis. URLs are the publisher's canonical addresses: nrel.gov did not resolve from the compilation environment, so NREL documents were retrieved through a mirror host and verified against their own title page and suggested citation before being recorded.

Low 16.4 USD/kWdc-yr is the ATB utility-scale FOM of 22 USD/kWac-yr for 2023 divided by the ATB ILR of 1.34 (the utility page reports O&M per kWac), which matches the NREL Q1 2023 utility MMP of 16.58 USD/kWdc-yr. parameters.locator: Table 2 Input Parameters (System losses default 14 %; Inverter efficiency 96; DC/AC ratio 1.1); Section 11 System Losses, Table 6 (soiling 2, shading 3, snow 0, mismatch 2, wiring 2, connections 0.5, light-induced degradation 1.5, nameplate rating 1, age 0, availability 3; total 14 % via Eqn. 9); Section 12 Inverter Model
parameters.basis: Base 86 % is 100 minus the PVWatts V5 default system losses of 14 %, which by construction exclude inverter efficiency (a separate input) and temperature (modeled explicitly), the same boundary as the HOMER derating factor when temperature is modeled on the PV Temperature tab. Low 80 % is the Table 6 multiplicative stack re-run with soiling raised from 2 % to 8 % for a desert array washed monthly (1 - 0.92 x 0.97 x 0.98 x 0.98 x 0.995 x 0.985 x 0.99 x 0.97 = 19.3 % loss); it also matches the HOMER Knowledge Base advice to 'simply reduce the derating factor to 80% or 70%' for warm climates when temperature is not modeled. High 89 % is the same stack for a clean open ground-mount with shading 0.5 %, soiling 2 % and availability 2 % (10.9 % loss). The HOMER Pro 3.16 derating-factor page defines the factor and lists soiling, wiring, shading, snow cover and aging as its content but prints no default; the 80 % HOMER default named in the brief could not be read on any HOMER page opened and is carried only as a Knowledge Base user example.
parameters.regional_note: GCC soiling figures, read from the papers' abstracts through the OpenAlex and Crossref APIs because mdpi.com returns HTTP 403 to every fetch route tried. (1) 'The Impact of Soiling on PV Module Performance in Saudi Arabia', Energies 2022, https://doi.org/10.3390/en15218033: 'Depending on the local environment and other factors, the PV performance has been reduced by somewhere between 2% and 50%. A single sandstorm reduced the module power output by 20%. As revealed in Dhahran, the PV module was exposed to an outdoor environment and not cleaned for 6 months resulting in a power drop of more than 50%. It is strongly advised to clean PV panels once a month or fewer'. (2) 'Quantification of PV Power and Economic Losses Due to Soiling in Qatar', Sustainability 2021, https://doi.org/10.3390/su13063364, Qatar University solar facility, Doha: 'without cleaning, soiling reduced the output power by 43% after six months of exposure to an average ambient dust density of 0.7 mg/m3', about 7 percent per month on average. (3) 'Effect of Soiling on Solar Photovoltaic Performance under Desert Climatic Conditions', Energies 2021, https://doi.org/10.3390/en14030659, 2.0 MWp car-park plant in Oman: cleaned output 1460 kW at noon, 1390 kW after one week, 1196 kW after three weeks and 904 kW after five weeks at the same irradiance; 'a soiling-percentage of 7.5% reduced the monthly electricity generation (307 MWh) by 5.6%'. (4) 'Seasonal Soiling Rates and Cleaning Optimization for PV Systems in Saudi Arabia: Arar Desert Climate', Energies 2026, https://doi.org/10.3390/en19184373: PVsyst scenario study, economic cleaning interval 60 to 90 days in the base case, 45 days under a high tariff. The per-month Saudi figures shown in search snippets (7 percent per month at Dhahran; 4 to 15 percent per month at Arar) were not read on a page and are not carried here.

parameters.locator: Generator struct docstring and constructor: installed_cost_per_kw = off_grid_flag ? 880 : only_runs_during_grid_outage ? 650.0 : 800.0 (master branch as fetched 19 Sep 2026)
parameters.basis: REopt's documented installed cost for a diesel generator is USD 800/kW when the unit is grid-connected and may run at any time (the hybrid case here), USD 650/kW when it only runs during grid outages, and USD 880/kW off-grid; the boundary is installed cost of the genset, and no dollar-year is stated in the file read. High 1,810 is the EIA / Sargent & Lundy 2020 Case 4 total overnight cost (2019 USD) for a 21.4 MW net natural-gas RICE plant (4 x 5.6 MW, with SCR, buildings, gas and electrical interconnection, owner's costs and 8 percent contingency), which is a full utility-plant boundary rather than a genset package, so despite its scale it sits above the genset figures and is used as the ceiling. The NREL Distributed Generation cost page with its diesel row could not be opened (nrel.gov returned no DNS record from this environment), so the base rests on REopt rather than that page.

parameters.source_title: Caterpillar, Cat 3512 Diesel Generator Sets, Prime-DCP 50 Hz spec sheet LEHE20483-00 (06/21)
parameters.locator: Page 2 of 4, Package Performance, Fuel Consumption: 1020 ekW / 1275 kVA rating, 100 percent load with fan 256.1 L/hr (75 percent 196.6, 50 percent 136.3, 25 percent 78.2); page 4 of 4, Fuel Rates: fuel oil 35 deg API, LHV 42,780 kJ/kg, 850 g/litre, per ISO 3046-1
parameters.basis: Generator-terminal efficiency at rated prime load: 256.1 L/h x 0.850 kg/L x 42.780 MJ/kg / 3.6 = 2,586.8 kW of fuel energy, so 1020 / 2586.8 = 39.4 percent for the 1020 ekW Cat 3512 at 1500 rpm (the 920 ekW rating gives 234.1 L/h and 38.9 percent); the Cummins C1100D5 (800 kWe prime, 202 L/h at full load, DS36-CPGK 08/19) gives 39.2 percent on the same fuel basis and 40.0 percent on 0.83 kg/L and 43 MJ/kg, which sets the high of 40. Low 32 is REopt's default electric_efficiency_full_load of 0.322 for a generic diesel generator, with HOMER's documented worked example (75 kW, 22.5 L/h at full load and 10.5 L/h at 25 kW, 820 kg/m3, 43.2 MJ/kg, giving intercept coefficient 0.06 and slope 0.24 L/hr/kW and 33.9 percent at full load) just above it. A least-squares HOMER fuel curve fitted to the four Cat points is slope 0.233 L/hr/kW output and intercept 18.3 L/h, that is 0.018 L/hr/kW rated. The HOMER default intercept and slope of about 0.08 and 0.25 L/hr/kW quoted in the brief were not found on any HOMER Pro 3.16 page opened (generator, fuel curve, slope, intercept, efficiency curve, knowledge base) and are not used.
